result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Beta]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Beta regression family with logit link. twitter-card: title: >- [Beta]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Beta regression family with logit link. title: "[Beta]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Beta regression family with logit link. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Beta regression family with logit link. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L14-L283){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature Beta(phi=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Beta family models a continuous response strictly between 0 and 1 — for example rates, fractions, or proportions that are not simply the ratio of successes to a known number of trials (in which case `Binomial` is usually more appropriate). It parameterizes the Beta distribution by its mean `mu` and a precision parameter `phi`, so that larger `phi` yields a tighter distribution around `mu` for fixed mean, analogous to the role `theta` plays in `NegativeBinomial`. The logit link keeps the fitted mean within `(0, 1)` and gives coefficients the same log-odds interpretation as in `Binomial` regression. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [phi]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fixed precision parameter, must be positive if provided. If `None` (the default), precision is treated as unknown and estimated from the data via the scale parameter (`phi = 1 / scale`); in that case `scale_known` is `False`. Passing a fixed `phi` is useful when the precision is known a priori or should not be re-estimated. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The link is the logit function: $$ g(\mu) = \log\!\left(\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}\right) $$ The variance function is $$ V(\mu) = \frac{\mu(1-\mu)}{1+\phi}, $$ so larger `phi` (higher precision) shrinks the variance for a given mean. The deviance is twice the difference between the saturated and fitted log-likelihoods, $$ D(y, \hat\mu) = 2 \sum_i \left[ \ell(y_i; y_i) - \ell(y_i; \hat\mu_i) \right], $$ where $\ell$ is the Beta log-density parameterized by $(a, b) = (\mu \phi, (1-\mu)\phi)$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to a proportion response with a smooth mean trend: ::: {#1df33306 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 200 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = expit(np.sin(x)) phi = 20.0 y = rng.beta(mu * phi, (1 - mu) * phi) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Beta()) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Beta(link='logit') Inference: REML Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err t value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.0188 0.0323 0.583 0.5603 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 6.22 7 366.621 < 1e-16 Total EDF: 7.22 Scale est: 0.047158 Deviance: 9.0913 Null dev: 27.9173 Dev. expl: 67.4% GCV score: 0.048923 AIC: -338.54 BIC: -314.74 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [scale_known](#scale_known){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Whether the precision parameter `phi` is fixed rather than estimated. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the precision parameter `phi` is fixed rather than estimated. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns `True` when a fixed `phi` was supplied at construction, and `False` when `phi` is `None` and must be estimated from the data during fitting. This determines whether `GAM.fit()` treats `phi` as a nuisance parameter to be estimated. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [deviance()](#deviance){.doc-function [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L172-L192){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature deviance( y, mu, *, weights=None, ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total (weighted) deviance. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for `mu`: `y` clipped strictly inside `(0, 1)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L262-L278){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Since the logit link is undefined at `0` and `1`, values are clipped to `[0.01, 0.99]` to avoid infinite linear predictors on the first P-IRLS iteration. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting values for `mu`, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the logit link: $\eta = \log(\mu / (1-\mu))$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L83-L96){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link(mu) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`; clipped to `(0, 1)` before transforming. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor (log-odds) values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the logit link: $g'(\mu) = 1 / (\mu(1-\mu))$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L113-L127){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`; clipped away from `0` and `1`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Derivative values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse logit link (logistic sigmoid): $\mu = 1 / (1 + e^{-\eta})$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L98-L111){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor (log-odds) values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`, always in `(0, 1)`. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Beta log-likelihood parameterized by mean `mu` and precision `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L194-L227){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature log_likelihood( y, mu, scale, *, weights=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The precision used is the fixed `phi` supplied at construction if set, otherwise `1 / scale`. Each observation's log-density is evaluated using shape parameters $(a, b) = (\mu \phi, (1-\mu)\phi)$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Used to derive `phi = 1/scale` when no fixed `phi` was supplied at construction. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total log-likelihood. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate Beta-distributed response values with mean `mu` and precision `phi`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L239-L260){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature simulate( mu, scale, rng, ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean (fitted values), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Used to derive `phi = 1/scale` when no fixed `phi` was supplied at construction. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `numpy.random.Generator` instance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation Beta deviance contributions. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L149-L170){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature unit_deviance( y, mu, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes a Binomial-like deviance form $d_i = 2 \left[ y_i \log(y_i/\hat\mu_i) + (1-y_i)\log((1-y_i)/(1-\hat\mu_i)) \right]$, used as a convenient goodness-of-fit measure on the `(0, 1)` scale. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values in `(0, 1)`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Per-observation deviance contributions, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Beta variance function: $V(\mu) = \mu(1-\mu) / (1+\phi)$ up to the `1+phi` scaling. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L129-L147){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This method returns the mean-dependent part $\mu(1-\mu)$; the precision-dependent scaling by `1/(1+phi)` is folded into the working weights elsewhere in the fitting loop. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Variance values $\mu(1-\mu)$, shape `(n,)`. :::
